evidence_quotes.section1_opening: Rep confirms phone number and email, mentions email will be sent over, but never delivers the quid pro quo frame ('10–15 minutes, you can walk away with a quote you can depend on, does that sound good?'). No explicit time-box or dependable-quote promise.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing: 'Do you have any questions or concerns you would like answered on this call?' — but this comes only after the rep has already gathered the origin address, unit, apartment details, floor, square footage, and parking distance. Amy states no particular concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised no concerns to follow up on; stated 'No, not particularly. I've moved a lot so it, this is old at for me.'
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised, so no reflection opportunity.
evidence_quotes.logistics_gathered: Rep covered: property type (apartment), floor (first floor at origin, second floor at destination), number of bedrooms (2), square footage (850 origin, 1200 destination), walking distance to truck (50 feet, later clarified could be less), special items (L-shaped desk, entertainment center, TV, heavy furniture), fragile items (TV 40-inch), elevator access (destination), parking garage access (destination). Full discovery of all seven logistics items.
evidence_quotes.packing_services: Never offered. Rep did not ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count: Asked and answered. Rep: 'As far as a box count, so it took for call box count for a one bedroom is about fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you feel like you would fall within that range?' Customer: 'I would say it's probably gonna be somewhere between fifty and a hundred boxes.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep anchors and personalizes: 'A normal one bedroom. The size usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours but I think it's heavier furniture the drive from Denton to Frisco and then possibility of that elevator definitely put you in that five and a half hour range.' Anchored (2.5–3.5 hrs baseline for typical one-bedroom) and personalized (heavier furniture, drive distance, elevator access push to 5.5 hrs). No dollar amount given.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Partial. Rep delivers: 'The way the clock works the time starts, as soon as we get on site open that contract, you didn't have us for as long as you need us. You do have a two and a half hour minimum. Once we go over that minimum, the time is prorated in the fifteen minute increments and then everything is included in our hourly rate, gas and truck taxes and insurance, and then all rap pads and bands protect items when being moved and all tools for assembly and disassemble.' This covers the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments, plus all-inclusive framing. No explicit trip fee or overnight fee disclosure, but pricing structure ('everything included in hourly rate') implies transparency. No 'not a guess' commitment language.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or waits for customer affirmation after the estimate. Rep moves directly to: 'Right, and I'm gonna go ahead and send over this email to you and then if you do have any questions or concerns leading up to the move, please don't hesitate to reach out.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Never mentioned. No reference to On-Time Guarantee, discount terms, or starting to discount if late.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage: Never mentioned. No reference to No Worries Damage Coverage, $2,000 coverage, no deductible, or built-in framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or close the loop on the Two Promises. Rep says 'if you do have any questions or concerns leading up to the move, please don't hesitate to reach out' — a handoff, not a loop closure.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep: 'Do you have any questions or concerns that you would like answered like, besides, now that we've kind of gone over everything. Do you have any other questions for me while you have me on the line?' This is phrased as a generic 'any other questions' not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' Customer: 'Nope.'
evidence_quotes.catch_all: Not asked. Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Rep does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable variant. Rep ends with 'I'm gonna go ahead and send over this email to you' — no explicit ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: Not mentioned. No reference to rate lock or no-deposit terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. Rep does not confirm date, phone number, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes. The call ends with email handoff; no booking is confirmed on this call.

top_strength: Brianne gathered comprehensive logistics details efficiently — property types, floor levels, square footage, special furniture, fragile items, elevator access, and parking constraints — all without rushing, which sets up accurate scoping.
coaching_note: This call skips the entire close: no quid-pro-quo frame in the open, no explicit ask for the business in Section 7, no Two Promises delivered, and no booking confirmation — the customer is handed off to email without ever confirming they want Einstein's help or locking in the October 8th date.
